name: Energy & Fusion
blurb: Intelligence is bottlenecked on electricity. The people building the models are personally funding the power to run them — fusion, factory-built fission, geothermal and thermal storage sited next to data centres.

name: Capital Rails & Markets
blurb: Payments, corporate spend, prediction markets, and a chartered bank purpose-built to lend against AI chips and private stock. Founders building the plumbing their own ecosystem runs on.

name: Compute & Silicon
blurb: The picks and shovels of the current paradigm: transformer-specific ASICs, sovereign GPU clouds, and vertically integrated power-plus-datacentre builders.

name: Preventive Health
blurb: Continuous measurement of healthy people rather than episodic treatment of sick ones. Small, young, and almost entirely founder-built — the consumer-facing edge of the longevity thesis.

name: Longevity & Reprogramming
blurb: Partial epigenetic reprogramming to reverse cellular age. Funded off tech founders' personal balance sheets rather than pharma, and now entering first human trials.

name: AI for Science
blurb: Closing the loop between hypothesis and experiment — automated laboratories where models propose, robots run, and results retrain the model overnight. The bet that AI's real prize is discovery, not chat.

name: Physical AI & Robotics
blurb: Foundation models for bodies. The West is pricing the general-purpose control layer; China is shipping roughly nine in ten of the world's actual humanoid units.

name: Autonomy & Mobility
blurb: Ground autonomy, finally shipping at scale. Capital has consolidated hard into a few winners while the long tail pivots to licensing its stack.

name: World Models & Simulation
blurb: Systems that model physical reality rather than text. The clearest 2026 thesis shift — the argument that language was a detour and the next layer worth owning is a simulator of the world.

name: Orbital Industry
blurb: Space as an industrial site rather than a destination — reusable lift, orbital logistics, pharmaceutical manufacturing, power beamed down, and now the argument that data centres belong off-planet.

name: Frontier Intelligence
blurb: The model labs. The two most valuable private companies on earth sit here, and a Chinese open-weight front rank has arrived at a fraction of the price.

name: AI-Native Software
blurb: Applications assumed to be commodity two years ago that turned out to have the fastest revenue ramps in software history. The operators' most conventional bets.

name: Post-Digital Compute
blurb: Machines that abandon deterministic digital logic altogether — thermodynamic sampling, analog in-memory compute, photonic quantum. Tiny cheques, government interest, and no consensus on which physics wins.

name: Neural Interface
blurb: Bandwidth between brains and machines. Split between invasive implants with patients today and non-invasive bets that the interface should be chemical or acoustic, not surgical.

name: Defence & Autonomy
blurb: Software-defined weapons, autonomous vessels and hypersonics. The most politically loaded theme on the board and the fastest-compounding by valuation — now with a European champion.

name: Earth Systems
blurb: Deliberate intervention in planetary systems — AI-guided mineral discovery, reinvented cement, and the first commercial attempts at dimming the sun. The most contested theme here, and the least capitalised.
